name: DeepSeek
subcategory: frontier open-weights LLMs (V3/V4, R1) and low-cost API
origin_detail: Spun off on 2023-07-17 from the AI research unit of High-Flyer, a Chinese quantitative hedge fund (unit announced 2023-04-14). Founder and CEO Liang Wenfeng held a 78% stake through two holding companies as of July 2026; the company was owned and funded by High-Flyer until its first external round in 2026.
openness_notes: Initial 1: early weights (DeepSeek-Coder, Nov 2023; DeepSeek-V3, Dec 2024) came under DeepSeek's own model licence, with code under MIT. Current 3: from R1 (2025-01-20) the weights themselves are MIT, explicitly allowing commercial use, modification and distillation; V3.1 (2025-08-21), V3.2 (2025-12-01) and V4-Pro (April 2026) are also MIT. Training data are not released, so this is open weights under an OSI licence rather than fully open science. The hosted chatbot and API are proprietary services.

license_history.license: DeepSeek model licence (custom) for weights; MIT for code

license_history.note: DeepSeek-V3 (Dec 2024): 'The use of DeepSeek-V3 Base/Chat models is subject to the Model License'; commercial use supported.
Released 2025-01-20 (paper 2025-01-22); permits commercial use and 'distillation for training other LLMs'. Distilled Qwen/Llama variants keep their base licences.
V4 preview 2026-04-24 (paper 'Apr 26'); V4-Flash full release 2026-07-31, V4-Pro 2026-08-13; V4.1-Flash 2026-09-10. Licence confirmed for V4-Pro.

relicensing_events.to: MIT (weights and code), from R1 onward
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Combined with low cost, the MIT release triggered the January 2025 market shock and made DeepSeek weights a base for widespread fine-tuning and distillation.

funding_as_of: 2026-05 (Series A only; the Oct 2026 round's amount is not confirmed: a headline says the round doubled to 100bn yuan)
risk_events: 2025-01-27: R1 release sparked a 17% fall in Nvidia shares (close $118.58) and a loss of close to $600B of market value, the biggest single-day drop in US history; DeepSeek topped ChatGPT as the most-downloaded free app on the US iOS App Store

US National Defense Authorization Act for FY2026 directs removal of DeepSeek and High-Flyer AI from Defense and Intelligence Community devices (research exceptions); Australia bans DeepSeek on government systems
Geopolitical/export-control exposure as a Chinese lab; reported Meta frustration that R1 drew on Llama's architecture fed Meta's turn to closed models (see meta.json)
2026-07: Bloomberg reported IPO preparations, with a listing as soon as 2027
robustness: Small (396 employees, 2026) but now well capitalised: a $7B Series A at a $52B post-money valuation (May 2026, per the FT) and a further round at a $70B pre-money valuation completed in October 2026 (SCMP, The Standard). Because every major model since R1 is MIT-licensed, its work survives independently of the company; dependence on a founder-controlled hedge fund and Chinese regulation are the main risks.
physical_science_relevance: MIT-licensed reasoning models that can be run locally are usable for scientific and lab-automation tasks without data leaving the lab; DeepSeek has no dedicated science programme in the pages fetched.
openness_effect_assessment: Openness was DeepSeek's route to global relevance: MIT-licensed weights at frontier quality and low cost made R1 the most-downloaded app in the US within a week and wiped about $600B off Nvidia in a day. Openness did not prevent commercial value. Within 18 months the company raised $7B at $52B and then a round at a $70B pre-money valuation, and it keeps releasing V4-class models under MIT. It also triggered strategic responses: US government-device bans and, per CNBC reporting, part of Meta's retreat from open frontier weights.
key_takeaway: DeepSeek is the strongest evidence in this group that open weights can shift market structure: an MIT-licensed model from a 2023 hedge-fund spin-off moved hundreds of billions in market value, prompted Sam Altman to say OpenAI needed 'a different open source strategy' (Jan 2025), before its Apache-2.0 gpt-oss release (Aug 2025), and fed Meta's rethink and still produced a $52-70B private valuation. Its openness is about weights and licence, not data, and its biggest risks are geopolitical rather than commercial. For the study, it shows that a permissive licence can be a competitive weapon for a challenger rather than a give-away.
